summary:
Attempt 2 fixed everything it was asked to, but the rewritten findings record draws a false conclusion from the Height batch.

**Checked and holding:**
- StallStacks self-test passes 13/13 and T005Batch passes 29/29; the hook builds with 0 errors.
- The seven new T005Batch fixtures and the two 10 ms StallStacks fixtures feed the shapes they claim.
- O-023 to O-029 are discharged where the builder says.
- height-2, trace-2 and render-2 match the doc's tables and verdicts. All 17 height-2 runs logged `"scanning":false` in their sized line.

**The new problem (major).** The hook now sets the height in a Loaded class handler. 860 is the window's default height, so this does nothing for the 860 arm. For the 644 arm it is a 216 px resize of a window that has already drawn once, and the work of redrawing at the new size lands after StartScan. That load-time resize, not the height, explains the difference the doc headlines.
- I ran four interleaved T-005 runs at 860 and 850 px.
- At 850 px, only 10 px from 860, the scan's first move waited 224.4 and 224.3 ms. At 860 it waited 343.6 ms; the other 860 run hit the ~1.3 s later-move stall.
- Across the second batches, the 860 px hardware runs had their first-move scan wait at 333.6–377.3 ms, and the 644 arm was at 106.6–243.4 ms.
- In height-2 runs 3, 6, 11 and 15 (644 px), the scan's longest wait was posted before the first move. That is work caused by the hook's own resize landing in the scan, which TreeMode's comment says cannot happen.

So the doc's 'the scan phase … says yes' (860 higher in 7 of 8, median 1.562), and its advice to run a scan-phase Height batch next, measure the hook's load-time resize and not the height. The same tool would reproduce the same result.

**A smaller gap (minor).** T005Batch's list of variables to strip from each run misses the `COMPlus_` aliases of the EventPipe settings. I confirmed that `COMPlus_EnableEventPipe=1` makes a .NET 10 process write a trace, that the strip pattern does not match it, and that the run inherits it.

Second round: One new defect this round: re-reading a traced batch with `-Reread` can record the wrong sampling interval and pick the wrong next step.

The verdict's sampling interval and its tracing-masks routing come only from the `-SampleMs` given to the current call. The rate the traced runs actually used is written in no summary line (runs.jsonl). So re-reading a batch that was run with `-SampleMs 10`, without repeating the flag, does two wrong things:
- verdict.json records `sampleMs: 1`;
- a masked result is sent back to 're-run at 10 ms' instead of to the in-process fallback.

The opposite mistake skips the 10 ms step the design requires. Each run's stacks-<n>.json already holds the real rate (`samplingNs`, read from the trace header), so the fix is small.

Nothing else broke under this round's inputs:
- **Reading summary lines:** Resolve-Lines copes with a line whose run number is missing, a run number stored as a different integer type, a duplicate line and a stray line.
- **Stripping variables:** the case-insensitive environment copy is materialised before any key is removed.
- **Absolute paths:** GetFullPath is applied against a location that WindowCases never changes.
- **Stack reader:** its exit and output are handled, and the cached Speedscope file is removed when it cannot be parsed.
- **Sampling spacing:** the observed-spacing figure is empty-safe.
- **Height hook:** the Loaded class handler runs before the window's own Loaded handler. If the window loads before the handler is registered, the run is refused loudly.

findings.claim:
The Height plan's two arms still differ by more than their height, and the findings record reads the difference as a height effect.

**What the hook does to each arm.** SizeOnLoad sets `window.Height` in a Loaded class handler, after the window's first render.
- **860 arm:** the XAML default is Height="860", so the set is a no-op.
- **644 arm:** it is a 216 px resize of a window that has already rendered. Its layout and render at the new size run after the instance OnLoaded has called StartScan.

**What follows in the 644 arm.**
- In 4 of 8 height-2 runs, a 106-225 ms UI-thread wait was posted before the probe's first move, and the first move itself came later.
- The first move no longer pays the first resize of a rendered window, which is what the 860 arm's first move pays.
- Changing the height by only 10 px reproduces the whole scan-phase gap. So the doc's reading is wrong: 'the scan phase alone, not decided on, says yes' (860 higher in 7 of 8, median 1.562), 'a Height batch on the scan phase, which the second batch suggests 860 px worsens'.
- The follow-on batch the doc prescribes would use the same hook and reproduce the same result.

**A false comment.** TreeMode's comment says 'no move or resize of the hook's lands between the scan's start and the first probe'. That is false for the low arm.
findings.evidence:
- **The resize:** tests/window/FsaWindowHook/TreeMode.cs:176-191 (SizeOnLoad sets Top/Height in a Loaded class handler), and the comment at :169-173.
- **The default height:** src/FsAnalyser.App/MainWindow.xaml:5 Height="860".
- **The 644 arm's early waits:** artifacts/sl080/height-2/runs.jsonl, 644 px runs, scan maxAt vs firstMoveAt: run 3 466/574, run 6 624/731, run 11 490/596, run 15 480/586. In the 860 runs, maxAt is always firstMoveAt+15.
- **Measured in this review:** four interleaved WindowCases.ps1 -Case T-005 runs on C:\ %TEMP%, with FSA_T005_SUMMARY and FSA_T005_HEIGHT set. Every sized line read `"scanning":false`.
  - 850 px: scan 224.4 ms (at 835, first move 836) and 224.3 ms (at 505/506); first move held 223 ms.
  - 860 px: scan 343.6 ms (at 748, first move 732), move held 134 ms; the other run hit the 1.3 s kind (1,400.6 ms).
- **The second batches:** every 860 px hardware run of height-2, trace-2 and render-2 except render-2 run 7 had a scan wait of 333.6-377.3 ms.
- **The doc's reading:** docs/design/SL-080-move-stall.md:71, 91-110, 170-171 and 185-189.
findings.fix:
In the doc, state that the scan-phase difference follows the hook's load-time resize (quote the 850-vs-860 runs), and withdraw 'says yes' and the scan-phase follow-on as written. Then make the arms equal at load before any scan-phase Height batch. Either:
- apply FSA_HOOK_HEIGHT before the window's first render, so neither arm resizes a rendered window; or
- give every arm the same load-time resize, for example by drawing both arms from heights other than the XAML default.

Fix the comment at TreeMode.cs:169-173 to match.

findings.claim: The R2-m4 strip list removes DOTNET_EventPipe*, DOTNET_EnableEventPipe and DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS, but not their COMPlus_ aliases. The .NET 10 runtime reads COMPlus_EnableEventPipe and COMPlus_EventPipe* exactly as it reads the DOTNET_ forms. A shell holding one of them traces every run's app, and the WindowCases pwsh as well, whatever the arm. Test-RunLine's new trace check looks only in FSA_T005_TRACE by pid, so it cannot see such a trace. An 'untraced' run is then silently sampled, which corrupts the tracing-masks comparison that O-028 set out to protect. This build already hit the DOTNET_ form of this leak once by accident.
findings.evidence:
- **The strip pattern:** tests/window/T005Batch.ps1, `$ArmVariables = '^(FSA_T005_|FSA_HOOK_|DOTNET_EventPipe|DOTNET_EnableEventPipe$|DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS$)'`, applied in Invoke-T005Run.
- **Measured in this review:** a .NET 10 process (pwsh) started with COMPlus_EnableEventPipe=1 and COMPlus_EventPipeOutputPath=<tmp>\leak-{pid}.nettrace wrote leak-20204.nettrace (3,399,010 bytes). `'COMPlus_EnableEventPipe' -match $ArmVariables` is False, and a new ProcessStartInfo inherited the variable from the shell.
findings.fix: Widen the pattern to cover both prefixes, for example `'^(FSA_T005_|FSA_HOOK_|(DOTNET|COMPlus)_(EventPipe|EnableEventPipe$)|DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS$)'`.

findings.claim:
On -Reread, the Trace verdict takes its sampling interval from whatever -SampleMs this call was given, not from the batch being read. No summary line records the rate: ConvertTo-T005Summary has no field for FSA_T005_SAMPLE_MS. Get-TraceVerdict records that parameter as verdict.json's sampleMs and routes tracing-masks on it. Two mistakes follow:
- Re-reading a batch that ran at -SampleMs 10, without the flag, records `sampleMs: 1` and sends a masked batch to 'run -Plan Trace once more with -SampleMs 10' rather than to the in-process fallback.
- `-Reread -SampleMs 10` on a 1 ms batch sends a first masking straight to the fallback, skipping the 10 ms re-run that the design and critique M5 require.

-Reread exists to recover a batch whose reading failed, so it is the path on which a person is least likely to remember the original flags.
findings.evidence:
- **Where the rate is taken from the parameter:** tests/window/T005Batch.ps1:290 (`if ($sampleMs -le 1) { 'run -Plan Trace once more with -SampleMs 10' } else { $fallback }`), :305 (`sampleMs = if ($sampleMs -gt 0) { $sampleMs } else { 1 }`), :357 (the `$sampleMs` parameter of Invoke-Plan), :522 (`$SampleMs` from the command line, including on -Reread).
- **Where the rate is not recorded:** tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 ConvertTo-T005Summary has no sampling field. FSA_T005_SAMPLE_MS is read only in New-T005Trace (:2734).
- **Where the real rate is available:** the reader's stacks-<n>.json carries `samplingNs` from the nettrace header (StallStacks.ps1 Invoke-Read).
findings.fix: In Get-TraceVerdict, take the interval from the traced runs' own stacks (samplingNs / 1e6; stop if they disagree), and fall back to -SampleMs only when no stack has one. Alternatively, write FSA_T005_SAMPLE_MS into the summary line and have Resolve-Lines refuse a -Reread whose -SampleMs differs from it.

The header documents 10,000,000 ns at 10 ms, and observedSampleMs is reported. Fixtures named-10ms and render-mixed-10ms (sampleMs 10) pass.

drift: The orderEffect flag is still symmetric: it fires when the first run of a pair is higher in ≥1 or ≥7 of 8 pairs (T005Batch.ps1 Get-HeightVerdict). The design said '≥7/8', and this extension is still not among the declared departures.

The new 'the scan had started before the hook sized the window' refusal in TreeMode.Sized cannot fire as written. `scanning` is read inside a Loaded class handler, which always runs before the window's instance OnLoaded that starts the scan. The only guard that can actually trip is `_sized is null` ('the window loaded before the hook could size it').

The Render rule gives 'render-thread-or-dwm-not-gpu' on a median ratio alone, with no floor on the batch's power. render-2 got that verdict with a detectable ratio of 5.41. The doc qualifies it ('rules nothing out'), but verdict.json does not.

docs/design/SL-080-move-stall.md:160 says 'in software the scan's first move was 68.4 and 90.2 ms'. Those are the scan phase's longest waits, posted 1.5-1.7 s after the first move (render-2 runs 1 and 5: maxAt 2531 and 2318, firstMoveAt 782 and 582). The first moves themselves held 29.7 and 28.6 ms.
